review_candidates.title: Director, Engineering and Interconnection
review_candidates.description: We are seeking a Director, Engineering and Interconnection to lead the owner's-side technical capability supporting Talen Energy's power generation, battery storage, and digital infrastructure development portfolio. The role is accountable for development-stage project engineering, technology and configuration decisions, technical diligence, and grid and transmission interconnection strategy. The Director will translate complex engineering and grid issues into clear decisions that improve safety, reliability, project economics, schedule certainty, and investment readiness. Reporting to the Chief Asset Development Officer, the Director supports opportunities from early site screening through Final Investment Decision and transition to execution. The portfolio includes simple-cycle peakers and combined-cycle facilities using aeroderivative and large-frame F- and H-class gas turbines; standalone and co-located battery energy storage systems; and powered-land and data center projects requiring large-load interconnection and resilient power delivery. The role works across Talen's development functions and with PJM, transmission owners, utilities, OEMs, EPC contractors, the owner's engineer, and technical consultants. Detailed design and specialized studies may be external, but this role retains accountability for technical strategy, standards, decisions, risk, deliverable quality, and consultant performance. Key Responsibilities Build and lead the Engineering & Interconnection function, including development-stage standards, design criteria, stage-gate deliverables, review protocols, consultant governance, technical reporting, and scalable capability. Support Site Origination by screening interconnection points, transmission and utility constraints, site layouts, fuel and water interfaces, constructability, and technical fatal flaws. Lead concept design and configuration for simple-cycle, combined-cycle, BESS, and powered-land or data center projects. Evaluate technology tradeoffs involving output, efficiency, dispatch profile, emissions, water use, footprint, reliability, operating flexibility, lifecycle cost, and schedule. Direct preparation and review of design bases, heat and mass balances, one-lines, layouts, equipment lists, performance assumptions, utility requirements, and preliminary specifications. Provide engineering inputs needed for permitting, estimating, contracting, and investment decisions, including plant configuration, emissions-control and stack assumptions, water and wastewater concepts, noise sources, site layouts, and construction requirements. Lead technical evaluation and procurement support for gas turbines, battery systems, transformers, substations, switchyards, controls, and balance-of-plant systems, including technical scopes, proposal reviews, guarantees, lifecycle implications, vendor selection, and long-lead risks. Select, direct, and hold accountable the owner's engineer, power-system and interconnection consultants, and other engineering specialists. Set acceptance criteria, challenge assumptions, manage quality, budget, and schedule, and resolve multidisciplinary interfaces before they create project risk. Own engineering and interconnection work plans, budgets, schedules, assumptions, and risks. Develop or validate capital-cost estimates, operating assumptions, equipment lead times, contingencies, engineering maturity, and critical-path inputs for development and investment decisions. Develop interconnection strategies for generation, storage, and large-load projects, including point-of-interconnection and queue strategy, generation and load-service pathways, co-location or behind-the-meter configurations, phased energization, redundancy, and alignment with target service dates. Oversee interconnection applications, models, and studies; interpret results and quantify network upgrades, cost and schedule exposure, grid-performance requirements, security, milestone risk, and mitigation alternatives. Support technical provisions in related agreements. Monitor PJM, transmission-owner, utility, FERC, NERC, and industry requirements; perform technical due diligence for acquisitions, partnerships, site reuse, and equipment opportunities; establish readiness criteria for stage gates and FID; and hand approved projects to Program Delivery and Construction, with targeted support through commissioning and performance testing. Partner with Project Owners as the accountable technical lead for each opportunity, translating engineering and interconnection analysis into clear recommendations on project configuration, technical feasibility, interconnection pathway, cost and schedule implications, key risks and mitigation alternatives—providing the technical fact base and judgment needed to advance projects toward Final Investment Decisions. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or another engineering discipline relevant to utility-scale power generation and electric power systems. 10+ years of progressive experience in power generation, transmission, interconnection, project engineering, or energy infrastructure, including substantial responsibility for development-stage work on complex capital projects. Owner's-side, developer, owner's engineer, EPC, OEM, or utility experience advancing utility-scale projects from screening and concept design through front-end engineering, interconnection studies, FID, or notice to proceed. Direct experience with simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas-fired generation, including aeroderivative gas turbines and large-frame F- and H-class technologies, together with experience with utility-scale battery energy storage systems. Strong knowledge of generation and transmission interconnection processes, technical submissions, agreements, network upgrades, cost and schedule drivers, and grid-performance requirements in one or more organized ISO/RTO markets. Ability to understand, review, and challenge power-flow, short-circuit, dynamic or transient-stability, reactive-power, deliverability, and related power-system studies without relying solely on summary conclusions. Broad understanding of power-plant and power-delivery engineering, including mechanical systems, high-voltage systems, substations and switchyards, transmission interfaces, civil and structural design, controls, and plant utilities. Success managing owner's engineers, consultants, OEMs, and EPC contractors; validating cost, schedule, performance, and risk inputs; and communicating complex technical issues to executives and nontechnical stakeholders. Ability to travel regularly as required. Preferred Qualifications Professional Engineer license and/or an advanced degree in engineering, engineering management, or business. Direct experience with PJM interconnection processes, multiple PJM transmission owners, and projects in one or more PJM states; experience in adjacent competitive power markets is also valued. Experience with powered-land, hyperscale data center, or other large-load development, including utility-service strategy, large-load interconnection, redundant power delivery, phased energization, and on-site generation or storage. Experience with greenfield or brownfield development, existing-site reuse, project execution or operations, and common power-system analysis platforms and industry standards. Leadership Profile Owner-minded technical leader who accepts accountability for decisions, risk, and outcomes rather than simply coordinating consultants. Combines deep engineering judgment with business and capital-allocation awareness; understands that the best technical answer must also be financeable, permittable, constructible, operable, and competitive. Independent, intellectually rigorous, and decisive under incomplete information; tests assumptions, quantifies tradeoffs, recommends a path, and challenges weak conclusions before they become embedded in a project. Collaborative capability builder who works effectively with Project Owners and peer functions while developing standards, tools, talent, consultant networks, and institutional knowledge that improve portfolio quality and speed. Success Measures Timely, decision-quality screening of new opportunities, with material engineering and interconnection fatal flaws identified before significant capital or schedule commitments. Safe, reliable, technically competitive project configurations supported by credible design bases, performance assumptions, equipment strategies, capital costs, schedules, and lifecycle considerations. Disciplined execution of PJM, transmission-owner, and utility interconnection processes, with complete submissions, met milestones, transparent upgrade exposure, and effective mitigation of grid-related risks. Consistent technical readiness at stage gates and FID, with fewer late design changes, scope gaps, consultant rework, and engineering or interconnection surprises after capital approval, followed by complete handoffs to execution. High-quality performance by the owner's engineer and other consultants, supported by repeatable standards, clear technical communication, strong cross-functional alignment, and credible external relationships. review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191-member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The Ebola outbreak, declared mid-May 2026, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with hundreds of suspected cases and hundreds of deaths reported across Ituri, South Kivu and North Kivu provinces. It began with clusters of unexplained deaths in early May and is spreading in a context of weak health systems, population movement, insecurity, and community mistrust, which together increase the risk of sustained transmission and cross-border spread to neighbouring countries such as Uganda and South Sudan. The absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment for this strain makes the outbreak particularly complex and heightens the urgency of rapid containment. IFRC is scaling up a national society‑led response centred on community engagement, surveillance, and infection control, supported by an emergency appeal. Red Cross volunteers are mobilized in affected areas to conduct door‑to‑door awareness, counter misinformation, encourage early care‑seeking, and support safe and dignified burials, key to breaking transmission. At the same time, the IFRC is coordinating closely with governments and partners, strengthening cross-border preparedness, mobilizing resources and surge capacity, and supporting logistics, infection prevention control, and community-based surveillance to contain the outbreak and reduce regional spread. Job Purpose The Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) Delegate will support the National Societies (NS) and IFRC Health and Operations teams to enhance the impact, reach and efficiency of emergency response operations through the integration and coordination of RCCE activities and approaches across the BVD response activities (and other emergencies as relevant). This includes designing and adapting risk communications using social and behavioural data and approaches, community engagement, strengthening feedback systems, engaging and coordinating RCCE activities with key external partners and evidence-based advocacy to elevate and address community concerns. The focus of the Delegate will be to provide technical support to the National Society and IFRC to strengthen contextually relevant, community-centred, evidence-based RCCE programming across the BVD response activities and other Health activities. They will work with RCCE partners to coordinate activities to ensure that communities have the health information they need to protect themselves and are included in the design and delivery of RCCE activities across sectors. The RCCE Delegate will have a specific focus on strengthening community feedback systems, ensuring community feedback and complaints are collected, analysed and acted upon by the sectors. As a key part of the health team, the role will work closely with Planning, Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (PMER) and Information Management (IM) counterparts to ensure all information and feedback from communities is effectively visualised, profiled within the operation, and used to inform strategic decision-making. Job Duties And Responsibilities Ensure that the BVD operation is implemented in accordance with Movement minimum actions, commitment, policies and guidelines relevant to risk communication, community engagement and accountability, while supporting continuity of essential health services and resilient community health systems. Support the planning, rolling out and adaptation of RCCE/CEA tools, SOPs, methodologies, trainings and activities based on community insights data to ensure they are suitable to the local context and BVD response dynamics. Ensure these are mainstreamed into the operation’s plan and budget to increase levels of engagement and accountability to people and communities. Ensures existing RCCE/CEA materials and resources including strategies, guidance notes, key messages, trainings and tools are properly shared and available at country/cluster level in a diversity of accessible and applicable formats and common languages. Support utilization of a range of applied behavioural approaches across BVD and health programmes in working with communities to identify community-led solutions to address challenges, improve behaviours and/or reduce the spread of infection, (strengthen protective health behaviours, increase trust in health services and reduce the transmission and impact of BVD). (Co-)Lead/participate in relevant inter-agency coordination groups, including health and RCCE coordination mechanisms to ensure communities remain at the center of the BVD response that their perspectives inform health policies, operational decisions and service delivery. Work closely with Ministry of Health, UNICEF, WHO and other partner RCCE focal points to share and promote action on community insights. Support National Society’s engagement with public health authorities and response partners to ensure Red Cross Red Crescent RCCE/CEA efforts are coordinated and recognized across the response. Support the setting up and/or strengthening of appropriate feedback methods and systems to enable real-time understanding and tracking of community perceptions, beliefs, concerns, rumours and complaints around BVD and health responses. Ensure feedback, community perceptions and insights are regularly analyzed, with support from Information Management, and shared with key operation teams and decision makers to inform action. Work with operation teams to ensure the most vulnerable groups have equal access to information channels and feedback mechanisms and participate in decision making processes. Support the implementation of appropriate community engagement initiatives to support the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), sexual and gender-based violence and survivor-centered approaches (in coordination with Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) and Human Resource teams. Design and facilitate the training of staff and volunteers on code of conduct, health promotion, good communication skills, feedback collection, sensitive handling of complaints and ensuring that feedback is acted upon.
